summary:
All three frames were reached and captured (sig prefix v-auth-). Reached by direct URL, every frame is genuinely excellent: sigdiff reports 34/34 (Login, Welcome Back) and 9/9 (Splash) design rows present, 0 missing, 0 positional/type differences, and the only differing rows are the documented D015 equivalences (two washes + mark halo radius 50%→-, four 2px stars 50%→1px, the 40px arrow 50%→20px). A 2x pixel diff of design vs app over y54..838 is worst Δ4 (Splash), Δ6 (Login), Δ6 (Welcome Back) — effectively pixel-identical, and the artwork is visibly present in every PNG (laurel, halo, both provider marks, arrow, stars, grain). The cold-open path `/` → `/splash` → `/sign-in` also lands pixel-clean on Login (Δ6) with no Back row, so that rework holds up.

BUT the report verified `03 · Welcome Back` only at its own URL. Driven the way the bundle designs it — `02 · Login` footer "Already have an account? Sign in" → `/welcome-back` — the board loses ALL THREE radial washes (top warm wash, low wash, and the laurel's 190 halo). The signature is still clean and 0-missing; only the PNG shows it. This is exactly the failure mode the brief's SVG-trap section warns about, and it is the group's one real defect. Cause: `Wash` in src/components/auth/kit.tsx takes a hard-coded gradient id ('ad-warm', 'ad-low', 'ad-mark'), expo-router keeps `/sign-in` mounted under the pushed screen with `display:none`, so the document carries two `<radialGradient id="ad-warm">` and `url(#ad-warm)` binds to the first — the hidden one — which paints nothing. Verified in the DOM: 6 radialGradients, the first three inside a display:none subtree. It persists at 4s, so it is not a transition. Same root cause hits `/sign-up?step=form` and the address/password/verify boards pushed over a door (D047 screens). It resolves itself on `router.back()` (the duplicate unmounts). This is a web-build defect — react-native-svg scopes defs per Svg root on iOS/Android — but it corrupts this run's own verification method for every auth board reached the designed way, and the fix is one line (useId()-derived ids).

Two capture/deliverable notes for the next pass: (1) the doors are NOT interactive at networkidle — tap() silently no-ops for roughly the first 1.5 s, which is almost certainly how the implementing agent's own driven check missed this; every recipe needs `await __sleep(1500)` first. (2) `.vicifull/recipes/auth.json` did not exist (nine other groups had written theirs); I have written it, including the failing-path recipe. Minor report inaccuracy: Welcome Back differs from Login in five strings, not four (title, subtitle, email row, footer prefix, footer link) — the code has all five right.

findings.element: the top warm background wash, div left:82 top:120 230×230, radial-gradient(closest-side, rgba(226,190,140,0.13), rgba(226,190,140,0) 72%)

findings.design: painted — sampled at canvas 196,235 the frame reads 72,61,47
findings.app: not painted — the same point reads 24,23,22 when the board is reached by tapping Login's "Already have an account? Sign in" (it reads 75,65,48 at the direct /welcome-back URL)
findings.note: src/components/auth/kit.tsx:82-94 + :116. `Wash` hard-codes the gradient id, `/sign-in` stays mounted display:none under the pushed screen, so `url(#ad-warm)` resolves to the hidden duplicate. DOM probe after the push: 6 radialGradients, first 3 inside a display:none subtree. Not the D015 border-radius equivalence — the box is right, the paint is gone. Persists at 4000ms. Repro: shot.mjs app "/sign-in" --do='await __sleep(1500); await tap("Already have an account? Sign in")' --wait=1400 (sig v-auth-a-wb4).

findings.design: the brief makes the per-group capture recipe part of the deliverable ("an accurate recipe — including the ones that failed — is part of the deliverable")
findings.app: the file did not exist; day/funnel/logs/medallions/settings/slip/sos/today/weeks all had theirs. I have written it, including the 1500ms settle every driven auth recipe needs and the failing-path recipe that reproduces the wash bug.
findings.note: Related: tap() is inert against these boards for ~1.5 s after networkidle — three consecutive runs of `tap("Already have an account? Sign in")` with no settle did nothing at all, and one earlier run navigated. Any driven verification of this group without the settle silently verifies the wrong screen.
